raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On ROCm, DSA decode and MTP verify run their top-2048 + page transform through the top-k v2 kernel. At long contexts with 72 or more rows per rank, v2 takes 113 to 127 us per call on MI355X. This PR adds a single-pass Triton/Gluon selector that takes 58 to 82 us there, 1.5x to 1.9x faster. It is opt-in via `SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_TRITON=1` because it is slower than v2 at short contexts; see the table below.

## Modifications

- **New `kernels/ops/attention/dsa/triton_topk_transform.py`**: three launches whose shape depends only on the row count (CUDA-graph safe).
  - `est`: per row, samples about 8192 logits and bit-searches a threshold that leaves about 2 x topk elements above it. Rounding down admits more candidates, but a biased sample can still overestimate the full-row threshold; the selector handles candidate underflow explicitly.
  - `collect`: one pass over the logits on a persistent grid; keys at or above the threshold go to a per-row candidate buffer of 8192 entries.
  - `select`: the exact k-th largest key among the candidates, then exactly min(L, topk) slots through the compact page table (`real_page_table`, page_size 64). This is the table the v2 decode graph keeps, so it needs no page_size=1 table.
- **Exact fallback.** If a row has fewer than min(L, topk) candidates or overflows the 8192-entry buffer, `select` takes the k-th largest key over the whole row and emits from it. This path is slow and rare, but it keeps the result an exact top-k for any input.
- **Dispatch** (`dsa_topk_backend.topk_transform`): this path is used, instead of v2, for decode-shaped PAGED rows when all of these hold:
  - `SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_TRITON=1`;
  - ROCm;
  - 128 rows or fewer;
  - fp32 logits with unit column stride.
- The ROCm and opt-in guards run before importing the optional Gluon selector, so disabled/non-ROCm routes keep their existing dependencies.
- **Tie order.** When the k-th key has ties, which tied elements are taken depends on candidate arrival order. The set is always a valid top-k, but it is not deterministic across calls.
- **Tests** (`test/registered/amd/test_dsa_triton_topk_transform.py`) check against a torch reference, accepting either choice among boundary ties. Cases: random rows (1 to 128 rows, up to 300k), short rows, a row built to overflow the candidate buffer (only the exact path gets it right), an all-equal row, and a biased sample that admits only 256 candidates for top-2048. A separate CPU regression checks that disabled/non-ROCm routes do not import the optional kernel.

## Accuracy Tests

- **Kernel.** The top-k sets equal v2's on every row of the benchmark below (synthetic logits) and on real GLM-5.2 workset logits (48 to 84 rows, contexts up to 659k).
- **gsm8k.** GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP8 DP8 DP-attention, MTP with acceptance not simulated, 400 questions. This path: 0.953 (one server). Main on the same node and day: 0.943 / 0.945 / 0.932 / 0.930 / 0.920 (five servers). These prompts are short; this checks that nothing else changed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Kernel.** On MI355X:
- inputs: fp32 logits 1M columns wide, 6 rows per request with lengths ctx+1..ctx+6;
- one CUDA graph over 4 logits buffers; us per call, median.

| context | rows | v2 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32k | 24 / 48 / 96 / 128 | 18.1 / 18.3 / 19.2 / 19.1 | 33.7 / 34.3 / 38.7 / 39.7 |
| 120k | 24 / 48 / 96 / 128 | 27.5 / 34.0 / 47.6 / 49.9 | 35.2 / 37.9 / 46.4 / 51.3 |
| 400k | 24 / 48 / 72 / 96 / 120 / 128 | 41.0 / 52.9 / 113.0 / 117.5 / 126.6 / 120.8 | 39.9 / 48.7 / 58.1 / 68.5 / 78.0 / 82.0 |

On real workset logits (contexts 235k to 659k), 72 / 84 rows: v2 92.7 / 91.4 us, this PR 44.3 / 44.9 us.

**End to end, short context (where v2 is faster).**
- Setup: GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP8 DP8 with DP attention, MTP, simulated acceptance 3.61, 96 verify rows per rank.
- Benchmark: random 32k input / 1k output, concurrency 128.
- Result: median ITL is 14.11 to 14.15 ms with this path, against 13.93 to 13.95 ms on main, so it is 1.3% slower. That is why it is opt-in.
- The long-context end-to-end case (where the kernel is 1.5x to 1.9x faster) was not measured here.

## How to reproduce

```bash
python3 test/registered/amd/test_dsa_triton_topk_transform.py -v
SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_TRITON=1 SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.61 SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected \
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --dsa-prefill-backend triton --dsa-decode-backend triton \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-dp-attention \
  --max-running-requests 128 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32000 --random-output-len 1000 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 128
```

The selector was found with an automated kernel-optimization search. This PR moves it onto the compact page table, adds exact underflow/overflow fallback, and adds the opt-in dispatch and tests.

Temporarily moving this PR to Draft while fixing a candidate-underflow correctness case found during maintenance.

For a row of length 131072 with top-k 2048, place 256 scores of 100 at sampled positions and leave all other scores zero. The sampled threshold admits only 256 candidates. The current selector takes its exact whole-row fallback only when the buffer overflows, so it returns 256 valid slots and 1792 padding entries instead of 2048 valid slots. Running the actual `_topk_est` and `_topk_select` with Triton's CPU interpreter reproduces this failure; a 2048-candidate control passes. The interpreter check does not exercise the Gluon collector or GPU compilation.

The repair will use the existing exact fallback for candidate underflow as well as overflow, add an adversarial regression, and keep optional Gluon imports behind the ROCm/opt-in guards. GPU validation is being requested through the machine pool. This is a correctness follow-up to the existing PR, not a new performance claim.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,376 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Single-pass top-k(<= 2048) + page transform for DSA decode / MTP-verify rows
+(ROCm, <= 128 rows): est (Triton) -> collect (Gluon) -> select (Triton).
+
+  est     per row, sample ~8192 logits (64 probes of 128) and bit-search the
+          sample key that leaves ~OVER * topk elements above it in the full row
+          -> a per-row threshold (rounded down, so it only adds candidates);
+          program 0 also builds the chunk prefix.
+  collect ONE pass over the logits on a fixed persistent grid of row-aligned
+          chunks; every key >= threshold is appended to the row's candidate
+          buffer (CAND entries).
+  select  per row, the exact k-th largest key among the candidates, then
+          exactly min(L, topk) slots through the page table.  If a row has fewer
+          than min(L, topk) candidates or overflows CAND, it selects exactly from
+          the whole row instead (slow, rare), so the result is always an exact
+          top-k.
+
+Output order is not defined, and when the k-th key has ties the members chosen
+among the tied elements depend on candidate arrival order.  The launch shape
+depends only on the row count (CUDA-graph safe).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+from triton.experimental import gluon
+from triton.experimental.gluon import language as gl
+
+_T = 8192  # logits per collect chunk
+_GRID = 2048  # persistent collect programs
+_CAND = 8192  # candidates per row
+_OVER = 2  # candidate target, x topk
+_SMP_CH = 128  # probe length
+_SMP_NCH = 64  # probes per row
+MAX_ROWS = 128
+_CSTR = 64  # int32 gap between rows' counters
+_COLLECT_NW = 4
+_FALLBACK_BLOCK = 4096
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _sum_combine(a, b):
+    return a + b
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _okey(b):
+    # order-preserving int32 key of a float32 bit pattern
+    return tl.where(b >= 0, b, (~b) ^ (-2147483648))
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _topk_est(
+    logits_ptr,
+    lengths_ptr,
+    pref_ptr,
+    ctr_ptr,
+    stride_l,
+    rows,
+    CH: tl.constexpr,
+    NCH: tl.constexpr,
+    TOPK: tl.constexpr,
+    OVER: tl.constexpr,
+    T: tl.constexpr,
+    RMAX: tl.constexpr,
+    CSTR: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    r = tl.program_id(0)
+    # program 0 also builds the chunk prefix (was a separate 5 us dispatch)
+    if r == 0:
+        ro = tl.arange(0, RMAX)
+        msk = ro < rows
+        La = tl.load(lengths_ptr + ro, mask=msk, other=0)
+        cp = tl.cumsum((La + (T - 1)) // T, 0)
+        tl.store(pref_ptr + 1 + ro, cp, mask=msk)
+        tl.store(pref_ptr, 0)
+    tl.store(ctr_ptr + r * CSTR + 1, 0)
+    L = tl.load(lengths_ptr + r)
+    k = tl.minimum(L, TOPK)
+    span = tl.maximum(CH, L // NCH)
+    o = tl.arange(0, CH * NCH)
+    p = (o // CH) * span + (o % CH)
+    m = p < L
+    b = tl.load(logits_ptr + r.to(tl.int64) * stride_l + p, mask=m, other=-1)
+    key = _okey(b)
+    ns = tl.sum(m.to(tl.int32), 0)
+    t = tl.maximum(1, tl.minimum((OVER * k * ns) // L, ns))
+    thr = 0
+    if tl.sum((key >= 0).to(tl.int32), 0) < t:
+        thr = -2147483648
+    # bits 30..15 only: rounding the sampled threshold down can only add
+    # candidates. Sampling can still overestimate the full-row k-th key;
+    # the selector handles that case with its exact underflow fallback.
+    for i in tl.static_range(0, 16):
+        cand = thr + (1 << (30 - i))
+        if tl.sum((key >= cand).to(tl.int32), 0) >= t:
+            thr = cand
+    tl.store(ctr_ptr + r * CSTR, thr)
+
+
+@gluon.jit
+def _topk_collect(
+    logits_ptr,
+    lengths_ptr,
+    pref_ptr,
+    ctr_ptr,
+    ckey_ptr,
+    cidx_ptr,
+    rows,
+    stride_l,
+    T: gl.constexpr,
+    CAND: gl.constexpr,
+    RMAX: gl.constexpr,
+    GRID: gl.constexpr,
+    CSTR: gl.constexpr,
+    NW: gl.constexpr,
+):
+    # Thread-local compaction with a pinned layout: thread t of the CTA owns the R
+    # 16-byte vectors (a, t, 0..3) of the chunk. The slot of a selected element is
+    # base + (count of the threads before t) + (its rank inside thread t): per-thread
+    # sums and in-thread ranks are register ops, the NT-wide scan (one value per
+    # thread) is the only cross-thread step, and the scattered stores keep the load
+    # layout (no LDS round trip). Within-chunk order is a permutation -- free, since
+    # the selector's output order is unconstrained and cross-chunk order was already
+    # atomic arrival order.
+    NT: gl.constexpr = 64 * NW
+    R: gl.constexpr = T // (NT * 4)
+    L3: gl.constexpr = gl.BlockedLayout([R, 1, 4], [1, 64, 1], [1, NW, 1], [2, 1, 0])
+    LRT: gl.constexpr = gl.SliceLayout(2, L3)
+    L2: gl.constexpr = gl.BlockedLayout([R, 1], [1, 64], [1, NW], [1, 0])
+    L1: gl.constexpr = gl.BlockedLayout([1], [64], [NW], [0])
+    pid = gl.program_id(0)
+    ro = gl.arange(0, RMAX, layout=L1)
+    pref = gl.load(pref_ptr + 1 + ro, mask=ro < rows, other=2147483647)
+    total = gl.load(pref_ptr + rows)
+    a = gl.arange(0, R, layout=gl.SliceLayout(1, LRT))
+    t = gl.arange(0, NT, layout=gl.SliceLayout(0, LRT))
+    v = gl.arange(0, 4, layout=gl.SliceLayout(0, gl.SliceLayout(1, L3)))
+    va = gl.expand_dims(gl.expand_dims(a, 1) * (NT * 4) + gl.expand_dims(t, 0) * 4, 2)
+    loc = va + gl.expand_dims(gl.expand_dims(v, 0), 1)
+    for c in range(pid, total, GRID):
+        r = gl.sum((c >= pref).to(gl.int32), 0)
+        start = (c - gl.load(pref_ptr + r)) * T
+        L = gl.load(lengths_ptr + r)
+        thr = gl.load(ctr_ptr + r * CSTR)
+        idx = start + loc
+        # 16-byte-granular load mask (rows are 4-aligned and >= L wide, so the tail
+        # vector's extra elements are in-bounds); the exact `idx < L` gates selection.
+        # Buffer base = the kernel argument (uniform), row folded into the 32-bit offset
+        # (host asserts the logits fit in 2**31 bytes): a base derived from the reduced
+        # `r` is not provably uniform and every buffer op becomes a waterfall loop.
+        b = gl.amd.cdna3.buffer_load(
+            ptr=logits_ptr, offsets=r * stride_l + idx, mask=(start + va) < L, other=-1
+        )
+        key = gl.where(b >= 0, b, (~b) ^ (-2147483648))
+        si = ((idx < L) & (key >= thr)).to(gl.int32)
+        s_v = gl.sum(si, 2)
+        cnt = gl.sum(s_v, 0)
+        n = gl.sum(cnt, 0)
+        if n > 0:
+            base = gl.atomic_add(ctr_ptr + r * CSTR + 1, n, sem="relaxed")
+            # tt.scan only lowers on blocked layouts: L1 / L2 are the same thread maps
+            # as the slice layouts (no data movement).
+            cnt_b = gl.convert_layout(cnt, L1)
+            tb = gl.convert_layout(
+                gl.associative_scan(cnt_b, 0, _sum_combine) - cnt_b,
+                gl.SliceLayout(0, LRT),
+            )
+            s_vb = gl.convert_layout(s_v, L2)
+            rv = gl.convert_layout(
+                gl.associative_scan(s_vb, 0, _sum_combine) - s_vb, LRT
+            )
+            rk = gl.expand_dims(rv, 2) + (gl.associative_scan(si, 2, _sum_combine) - si)
+            p = base + gl.expand_dims(gl.expand_dims(tb, 0), 2) + rk
+            mm = (si != 0) & (p < CAND)
+            gl.amd.cdna3.buffer_store(key, ptr=ckey_ptr, offsets=r * CAND + p, mask=mm)
+            gl.amd.cdna3.buffer_store(idx, ptr=cidx_ptr, offsets=r * CAND + p, mask=mm)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _row_threshold(row_ptr, L, k, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+    """Exact k-th largest key of a whole row (31-step bit search over the row)."""
+    thr = 0
+    cnt0 = 0
+    for s in range(0, L, BLOCK):
+        o = s + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+        b = tl.load(row_ptr + o, mask=o < L, other=-1)
+        cnt0 += tl.sum(((o < L) & (_okey(b) >= 0)).to(tl.int32), 0)
+    if cnt0 < k:
+        thr = -2147483648
+    for i in tl.static_range(0, 31):
+        cand = thr + (1 << (30 - i))
+        c = 0
+        for s in range(0, L, BLOCK):
+            o = s + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+            b = tl.load(row_ptr + o, mask=o < L, other=-1)
+            c += tl.sum(((o < L) & (_okey(b) >= cand)).to(tl.int32), 0)
+        if c >= k:
+            thr = cand
+    return thr
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _topk_select(
+    ckey_ptr,
+    cidx_ptr,
+    ctr_ptr,
+    lengths_ptr,
+    logits_ptr,
+    stride_l,
+    page_ptr,
+    stride_p,
+    out_ptr,
+    CAND: tl.constexpr,
+    TOPK: tl.constexpr,
+    CSTR: tl.constexpr,
+    PAGE_SHIFT: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    r = tl.program_id(0)
+    n_all = tl.load(ctr_ptr + r * CSTR + 1)
+    L = tl.load(lengths_ptr + r)
+    k = tl.minimum(L, TOPK)
+    pt = page_ptr + r.to(tl.int64) * stride_p
+    out_cols = tl.arange(0, TOPK)
+    if (n_all < k) | (n_all > CAND):
+        # The sampled threshold was too high (underflow) or too low (overflow):
+        # select exactly from the whole row instead. Rare and slow.
+        row = logits_ptr + r.to(tl.int64) * stride_l
+        thr = _row_threshold(row, L, k, BLOCK)
+        base = 0
+        above = 0
+        for s in range(0, L, BLOCK):
+            o = s + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+            key = _okey(tl.load(row + o, mask=o < L, other=-1))
+            above += tl.sum(((o < L) & (key > thr)).to(tl.int32), 0)
+        room = k - above
+        eq_seen = 0
+        for s in range(0, L, BLOCK):
+            o = s + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+            key = _okey(tl.load(row + o, mask=o < L, other=-1))
+            gt = (o < L) & (key > thr)
+            eq = (o < L) & (key == thr)
+            eq_rank = eq_seen + tl.cumsum(eq.to(tl.int32), 0) - eq.to(tl.int32)
+            take = gt | (eq & (eq_rank < room))
+            ti = take.to(tl.int32)
+            pos = base + tl.cumsum(ti, 0) - ti
+            slot = (
+                tl.load(pt + (o >> PAGE_SHIFT), mask=take, other=0) << PAGE_SHIFT
+            ) + (o & ((1 << PAGE_SHIFT) - 1))
+            tl.store(out_ptr + r * TOPK + pos, slot, mask=take)
+            base += tl.sum(ti, 0)
+            eq_seen += tl.sum(eq.to(tl.int32), 0)
+        tl.store(
+            out_ptr + r * TOPK + out_cols,
+            tl.full((TOPK,), -1, tl.int32),
+            mask=out_cols >= base,
+        )
+    else:
+        n = n_all
+        o = tl.arange(0, CAND)
+        m = o < n
+        cb = r.to(tl.int64) * CAND
+        key = tl.load(ckey_ptr + cb + o, mask=m, other=-2147483648)
+        thr = 0
+        if tl.sum((key >= 0).to(tl.int32), 0) < k:
+            thr = -2147483648
+        for i in tl.static_range(0, 31):
+            cand = thr + (1 << (30 - i))
+            if tl.sum((key >= cand).to(tl.int32), 0) >= k:
+                thr = cand
+        gt = m & (key > thr)
+        gti = gt.to(tl.int32)
+        eq = m & (key == thr)
+        eqi = eq.to(tl.int32)
+        # one packed CAND-wide scan carries both ranks (each field < CAND <= 65536)
+        cs = tl.cumsum(gti + (eqi * 65536), 0)
+        rank_gt = (cs & 65535) - gti
+        rank_eq = (cs // 65536) - eqi
+        above = tl.sum(gti, 0)
+        room = k - above
+        take = gt | (eq & (rank_eq < room))
+        n_take = tl.sum(take.to(tl.int32), 0)
+        pos = rank_gt + tl.minimum(rank_eq, room)
+        idx = tl.load(cidx_ptr + cb + o, mask=take, other=0)
+        slot = (tl.load(pt + (idx >> PAGE_SHIFT), mask=take, other=0) << PAGE_SHIFT) + (
+            idx & ((1 << PAGE_SHIFT) - 1)
+        )
+        tl.store(
+            out_ptr + r * TOPK + out_cols,
+            tl.full((TOPK,), -1, tl.int32),
+            mask=out_cols >= n_take,
+        )
+        tl.store(out_ptr + r * TOPK + pos, slot, mask=take)
+
+
+def topk_transform_paged_triton(
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+    lengths: torch.Tensor,
+    page_table: torch.Tensor,
+    page_size: int,
+    topk: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Top-``topk`` of ``logits[row, :lengths[row]]`` mapped to physical KV slots
+    ``page_table[row, p // page_size] * page_size + p % page_size``; ``-1`` padded.
+
+    ``logits`` fp32 ``[rows, >= max(lengths)]`` with unit column stride,
+    ``page_table`` int32 ``[rows, pages]``.  ``rows <= MAX_ROWS`` and
+    ``rows * logits.stride(0) * 4 < 2**31`` (32-bit buffer offsets).
+    """
+    rows = logits.shape[0]
+    dev = logits.device
+    assert 0 < rows <= MAX_ROWS, rows
+    assert page_size & (page_size - 1) == 0, page_size
+    assert logits.dtype == torch.float32 and logits.stride(1) == 1
+    out = torch.empty((rows, topk), dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    ctr = torch.empty((rows, _CSTR), dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    pref = torch.empty((rows + 1,), dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    ckey = torch.empty((rows, _CAND), dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    cidx = torch.empty((rows, _CAND), dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    li = logits.view(torch.int32)
+    sl = li.stride(0)
+    assert rows * sl * 4 < 2**31 and rows * _CAND * 4 < 2**31
+    _topk_est[(rows,)](
+        li,
+        lengths,
+        pref,
+        ctr,
+        sl,
+        rows,
+        CH=_SMP_CH,
+        NCH=_SMP_NCH,
+        TOPK=topk,
+        OVER=_OVER,
+        T=_T,
+        RMAX=MAX_ROWS,
+        CSTR=_CSTR,
+        num_warps=8,
+    )
+    _topk_collect[(_GRID,)](
+        li,
+        lengths,
+        pref,
+        ctr,
+        ckey,
+        cidx,
+        rows,
+        sl,
+        T=_T,
+        CAND=_CAND,
+        RMAX=MAX_ROWS,
+        GRID=_GRID,
+        CSTR=_CSTR,
+        NW=_COLLECT_NW,
+        num_warps=_COLLECT_NW,
+    )
+    _topk_select[(rows,)](
+        ckey,
+        cidx,
+        ctr,
+        lengths,
+        li,
+        sl,
+        page_table,
+        page_table.stride(0),
+        out,
+        CAND=_CAND,
+        TOPK=topk,
+        CSTR=_CSTR,
+        PAGE_SHIFT=page_size.bit_length() - 1,
+        BLOCK=_FALLBACK_BLOCK,
+        num_warps=8,
+    )
+    return out

+"""The ROCm single-pass DSA top-k selector (triton_topk_transform.py) against a
+torch reference: an exact top-k (ties at the boundary may be broken either way),
+mapped through the page table, -1 padded; including rows whose candidate buffer
+underflows or overflows and must take the exact whole-row path."""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+
+PAGE, TOPK = 64, 2048
+
+
+def _skip_reason():
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.version.hip is None:
+        return "ROCm GPU required"
+    try:
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa import triton_topk_transform  # noqa: F401
+    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - build-environment dependent
+        return f"unavailable: {exc}"
+    return None
+
+
+SKIP = _skip_reason()
+register_amd_ci(est_time=60, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x")
+
+
+@unittest.skipIf(SKIP is not None, SKIP or "")
+class TestTritonTopkTransform(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa.triton_topk_transform import (
+            topk_transform_paged_triton,
+        )
+
+        self.fn = topk_transform_paged_triton
+        self.dev = torch.device("cuda", 0)
+
+    def _run(self, logits, lens):
+        rows, width = logits.shape
+        pages = -(-width // PAGE)
+        g = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(rows + width)
+        pt = torch.stack(
+            [torch.randperm(1 << 20, generator=g)[:pages] for _ in range(rows)]
+        ).int()
+        out = self.fn(logits, lens.to(self.dev), pt.to(self.dev), PAGE, TOPK)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        return out.cpu(), pt
+
+    def _check(self, logits, lens):
+        out, pt = self._run(logits, lens)
+        lg = logits.cpu()
+        for r in range(lg.shape[0]):
+            n = int(lens[r])
+            k = min(n, TOPK)
+            got = out[r]
+            sel = got[got >= 0]
+            self.assertEqual(sel.numel(), k, f"row {r}")
+            self.assertEqual(int((got == -1).sum()), TOPK - k, f"row {r}")
+            self.assertEqual(sel.unique().numel(), k, f"row {r}: duplicate slots")
+            # slot -> position through the (unique-per-row) page table
+            npg = -(-n // PAGE)
+            page_idx = {int(p): i for i, p in enumerate(pt[r, :npg].tolist())}
+            pos = torch.tensor(
+                [page_idx[int(s) // PAGE] * PAGE + int(s) % PAGE for s in sel]
+            )
+            self.assertTrue(bool((pos < n).all()), f"row {r}: slot past length")
+            if k == n:
+                self.assertEqual(sorted(pos.tolist()), list(range(n)), f"row {r}")
+                continue
+            vals = lg[r, :n]
+            kth = torch.topk(vals, k).values[-1]
+            self.assertTrue(bool((vals[pos] >= kth).all()), f"row {r}: below k-th")
+            self.assertEqual(
+                int((vals[pos] > kth).sum()), int((vals > kth).sum()), f"row {r}"
+            )
+
+    def test_random_rows(self):
+        g = torch.Generator(device=self.dev).manual_seed(0)
+        for rows, width in ((1, 4096), (6, 200_000), (48, 300_000), (128, 65_536)):
+            with self.subTest(rows=rows, width=width):
+                logits = torch.randn(rows, width, device=self.dev, generator=g)
+                lens = torch.randint(1, width + 1, (rows,), generator=None).int()
+                lens[0] = width
+                self._check(logits, lens)
+
+    def test_short_rows_select_everything(self):
+        logits = torch.randn(8, 4096, device=self.dev)
+        self._check(logits, torch.tensor([1, 100, 2047, 2048, 7, 0 + 5, 30, 1000]))
+
+    def test_candidate_overflow_takes_exact_path(self):
+        """A row whose sampled probes see only zeros while 5000 ones sit between
+        them: the sampled threshold admits the whole row (> CAND candidates), and
+        only the exact path returns ones."""
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa import triton_topk_transform as m
+
+        width = 1 << 20
+        logits = torch.zeros(2, width, device=self.dev)
+        span = width // m._SMP_NCH
+        probe = (torch.arange(width) % span) < m._SMP_CH
+        free = torch.nonzero(~probe).flatten()
+        logits[0, free[torch.randperm(free.numel())[:5000]]] = 1.0
+        logits[1] = torch.randn(width, device=self.dev)
+        self._check(logits, torch.tensor([width, width]))
+
+    def test_candidate_underflow_takes_exact_path(self):
+        """A biased sample admits only 256 candidates for top-2048. The remaining
+        valid selections must come from the exact whole-row path, not padding."""
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa import triton_topk_transform as m
+
+        width = 1 << 17
+        probes = torch.arange(m._SMP_CH * m._SMP_NCH, device=self.dev)
+        positions = (probes // m._SMP_CH) * (width // m._SMP_NCH) + (probes % m._SMP_CH)
+        logits = torch.zeros(1, width, device=self.dev)
+        logits[0, positions[:256]] = 100.0
+        self._check(logits, torch.tensor([width]))
+
+    def test_all_equal_row(self):
+        logits = torch.full((3, 100_000), 0.5, device=self.dev)
+        self._check(logits, torch.tensor([100_000, 50_000, 3000]))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+"""The opt-in selector must not require Gluon when its route is disabled."""
+
+import builtins
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsa import dsa_topk_backend
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=1, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "is_hip,enabled", [(False, True), (True, False), (False, False)]
+)
+def test_disabled_route_does_not_import_optional_kernel(monkeypatch, is_hip, enabled):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(dsa_topk_backend, "_is_hip", is_hip)
+    monkeypatch.setenv("SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_TRITON", "1" if enabled else "0")
+    original_import = builtins.__import__
+
+    def checked_import(name, *args, **kwargs):
+        if name == "sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa.triton_topk_transform":
+            raise AssertionError("Disabled top-k route imported the optional kernel")
+        return original_import(name, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(builtins, "__import__", checked_import)
+    # An inactive route must not inspect tensor metadata either.
+    assert dsa_topk_backend._use_triton_topk(None, 2048) is False
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))

Temporarily moving this PR to Draft while fixing a candidate-underflow correctness case found during maintenance.

For a row of length 131072 with top-k 2048, place 256 scores of 100 at sampled positions and leave all other scores zero. The sampled threshold admits only 256 candidates. The current selector takes its exact whole-row fallback only when the buffer overflows, so it returns 256 valid slots and 1792 padding entries instead of 2048 valid slots. Running the actual `_topk_est` and `_topk_select` with Triton's CPU interpreter reproduces this failure; a 2048-candidate control passes. The interpreter check does not exercise the Gluon collector or GPU compilation.

The repair will use the existing exact fallback for candidate underflow as well as overflow, add an adversarial regression, and keep optional Gluon imports behind the ROCm/opt-in guards. GPU validation is being requested through the machine pool. This is a correctness follow-up to the existing PR, not a new performance claim.

Maintenance update: rebased onto main `a133231d3140e081424d833caa0187f15d40dc3c`; current head `1061c298389facbdeaafced9891a5c7c9b399331`.

The temporary correctness Draft is resolved. The original actual GPU pipeline returns only 256 valid slots plus 1792 padding entries for top-2048 on the biased-sample case; the repaired pipeline returns 2048 unique valid slots and retains all 256 high-score entries. All five repaired GPU tests pass with zero skips. The original four tests passed but missed this bug. Run: `kf47872-20261102T1038Z-topk-underflow`, one MI355X/gfx950 GPU, public `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi35x-20261021`, Torch `2.11.0+rocm10.0.0`, Triton `3.8.0`. Kernel/test hashes match the committed head. The exact-module runner uses namespace/CI-registration shims for the older image; this is kernel validation, not a new server or performance measurement. The PR body records the repair, CPU/GPU validation and remaining limits.

Validation: Full-tree Ruff, scoped hooks and 32 CPU tests passed; actual-kernel interpreter controls passed; original GPU underflow reproduced and all 5 repaired MI355X GPU tests passed with zero skips.
